Regime Ladder · research scaffold

The framework, end to end

How option-component P&L is conditioned on market state: the data, the features, the five named states and how they are found, what a state looks like in the trader's terms, sub-states discovered inside them, shock detection, transition probabilities, the horizon ladder that is the product, the path model that extends it, and the gates that decide whether any of it earns its keep. Every picture is from synthetic data with known answers until Gates 2 and 3 replace them.

Status tags on each section: built · validated on synthetic means it exists in the repository and recovers known answers on synthetic data; designed · not yet built means specified in the plan but not written; hypothesis means an economic claim kept for testing, not a model input.

1The question and the number built · validated on synthetic

A market-making book in FX options is, at any moment, a portfolio of smile-vega-neutral components: ATM vega by tenor, 25-delta risk reversal, 10-delta fly. The desk's backtester reports what each component, entered fresh on any past day and hedged the way the desk hedges, earned on every day of its life. The question this framework answers is: what does one fresh unit of a component earn over the next 1, 3, 5, 10 and 20 days, on days that look like today?

EV(h | entry state)  =  average over past entries in that state of  [ cumulative net P&L to day h ]
                        held h days, no exit rule, hedged as the backtester hedges, cash per unit standard notional
Read it as the marginal expected earn of carrying one unit of this component for the next h days from today's state — a number to tilt composition with, not a trade signal. Short horizons are primary for a book that is re-cut continuously; the increments between horizons are how the number applies to inventory of mixed age.

Three design commitments follow from measuring it this way rather than estimating a daily rate per regime and adding days up: the exposure is right by construction because every observation starts from a fresh unit and ages through the backtester's own repricing; regime changes inside the window are already in the outcomes, so nothing is added for them and nothing can be double-counted; and the distribution — tails, probability of profit — is measured, not simulated.

2Architecture

3Data and integrity built · validated on synthetic

Two interfaces, nothing else downstream knows about the source. The trade-day table: one row per trade per day with pair, archetype, tenor, entry date, date, age, net P&L per unit notional, and where available the components (trade, delta hedge, vega hedge) and daily Greeks. The market frame: a daily, point-in-time panel of the surface by tenor, spot (daily and hourly), the other G10 pairs, and the cross-asset series the profile uses. Every build runs the integrity checks: ages consecutive from 1, no duplicates, dates after entry, components summing to total, a label for every entry date. A table that fails any of them produces no statistic.

Point-in-time rule. Every feature, characteristic and label for date t uses only what was available at the close of t. It is enforced mechanically, not by discipline: every feature function takes an asof argument and must pass the truncation test — computed with history cut at T, it must agree with the full computation on every date ≤ T. A feature that fails cannot be registered.

4State features built · validated on synthetic

State features answer "where are we now". They are trailing percentile ranks or z-scores of surface quantities, nothing centred, nothing full-sample. The starting set: ATM vol percentile, term-structure slope, risk-reversal stress, variance risk premium, spot-vol beta, realised term ratio. Four to six go into the labeller; with 5–15 independent regime episodes per pair, more overfit.

5Five named states: level × direction built · validated on synthetic

Three states on one stress axis — the first draft's design — fail in two specific ways. "Transition" is traversed in both directions, and vol rising from low and vol falling from high are opposite for every component. And post-crisis normalisation, where vol is high but falling and premia are rich, is where short vol and short wings earn most of their year; it is not a flavour of crisis. More states on the same axis would starve the cells. The answer is a second axis with few levels:

low · uprising
mid · uprising(crisis if coming from crisis)
high · upcrisis
low · flatcarry
mid · flatkeep previous
high · flatcrisis
low · downsettling(carry if already in carry)
mid · downnormalising(settling if coming from rising)
high · downnormalising

Rows: direction of the smoothed score (slope over 5 days, with its own thresholds and hysteresis). Columns: level (two boundaries with hysteresis). A few cells depend on the previous state so that carry drifting down is still carry and a rise that fizzles is settling, not normalising.

6The state finder built · validated on synthetic

Boundaries, direction thresholds, smoothing and hysteresis are not chosen by hand. calibrate_states takes the composite score over a training window and a forward outcome — the archetype's forward 5-day P&L where the backtester covers the window, forward surface change on the longer history otherwise — and does four things: estimates the two level boundaries by a two-kink regression of the outcome on the score; sets direction thresholds from the slope distribution; scores every combination of half-life, hysteresis and direction sensitivity by out-of-sample separation of the outcome (state means fitted on earlier folds, applied to later ones); and compares the three-state and five-state partitions on the same criterion, under a switch budget and a minimum-episodes rule. It returns a spec and a report. It does not decide; the owner does, at Gate 2.

Two more things the synthetic world taught the finder. Without a switch budget it chooses zero hysteresis and labels that flip every few days, because out-of-sample R² does not penalise flicker; with max_switches_per_year and a fewest-switches tie-break among near-best specs it lands close to the true switch rate. And states are calibrated on the ten-year surface while the ladder uses the five years the backtester covers, so state definitions and transition counts see roughly twice the episodes the P&L does.

7State profiles built · validated on synthetic

A named state is a region of a two-dimensional score. What it looks like is a different question, and the one a trader asks: what kind of rising is this? The characteristics vector answers it, daily and point-in-time, in three groups:

  1. Own pair: spot-vol beta and correlation, variance risk premium, term slope, risk-reversal and fly levels, vol-of-vol, jump frequency.
  2. Cross-pair: the share of G10 variance explained by the dollar factor (is this move USD-led or idiosyncratic?), average pairwise correlation.
  3. Cross-asset: 20-day correlation of the pair's spot return, and separately of its vol change, with equities, front- and long-end yields, oil, gold, the dollar index, a credit spread, equity vol and rates vol. The list is a config entry; add or change series freely.

The state profile is each characteristic's mean inside the state against all days, in standard deviations, ranked by how distinguishing it is; describe turns the top three into a phrase; today_placement says where today sits inside the state's own history.

  • carry — rr_level high (+0.8σ) · term_slope low (-0.8σ) · fly_level low (-0.8σ)
  • rising — vrp high (+0.5σ) · term_slope high (+0.4σ) · rr_level low (-0.2σ)
  • crisis — fly_level high (+1.9σ) · rr_level low (-1.8σ) · term_slope high (+1.7σ)
  • normalising — fly_level high (+0.8σ) · volofvol high (+0.7σ) · rr_level low (-0.7σ)
  • settling — corr_spot_oil high (+0.5σ) · term_slope low (-0.4σ) · vrp low (-0.4σ)

8Sub-state discovery built · validated on synthetic

Inside a named state, days are clustered on the standardised characteristics vector. A sub-state is allowed to exist only under three conditions: a k > 1 model is preferred; every cluster has at least five contiguous episodes; and models fitted on the first and second halves of the state's history agree on at least 70% of days. Fail any one and the state stands alone. Even then a sub-state is descriptive — shown on the card as context — until, separately, conditioning the ladder on it beats the parent state out of sample (benchmark layer 2b, Section 14). Names are generated from what distinguishes each cluster, not chosen in advance.

On real data the sub-states this is built to separate within rising are the ones traders already name: dollar-led risk-off (equities down, front end rallying, dollar factor dominant); rates-led (rates vol leading, dollar up with yields); an idiosyncratic pair event (dollar-factor share collapses); a carry unwind (funding pairs lead, vol co-moves, equities down); commodity- or EM-led. Discovery also doubles as a label-impurity detector: inside estimated carry on synthetic data it surfaced a cluster with low wings and low term slope that was, in truth, mislabelled settling.

9Shock detection designed · not yet built

The labeller is smooth by design and therefore late. Shock detectors are the fast path: they do not define the state, they move probability mass toward the next one and, in Phase 4, feed the regime probability vector π that drives the path model. Two quantities are kept separate because they answer different questions. The economic surprise is the day's return standardised by the implied daily vol marked before it: the move relative to what the market priced, the one that matters for option P&L. The physical variance forecast (GARCH or HAR) is a model of realised variance with its own innovation, used to compare a forward-RV path with the traded surface.

Bayesian online changepoint detection supplies P(run length < m) under an explicit observation model; a statistical changepoint in squared returns is not automatically a move between named states, so the blending rule into π is labelled a heuristic until the calibration test in Section 14 says otherwise. The final threshold is economic, not statistical: the ladder's response to recent shock size, and the kink in it, decides what counts.

10Transition probabilities built · validated on synthetic constant matrix designed · not yet built time-varying

A trade entered in one state lives through others. The horizon ladder measures that directly — transitions inside the window are in the outcomes — so for a fresh unit no transition model is needed and none is used. The transition matrix earns its place for three other things: explaining the ladder (how long does carry usually last from here?), the Phase 4 path model, and incorporating today's leading signals where today's propensity to move differs from the state's historical average.

Try it. Pick today's state and a pressure level; the fan is P(state at h) under the tilted matrix, with expected days in each state over the next 21 and P(crisis) at 5, 10 and 21 days. Holding pressure fixed for 63 days is a sustained-pressure scenario: in the real model each covariate has a declared future path — frozen, decaying, calendar-known, or simulated.

11Leading features and stored energy hypothesis

State features say where we are; leading features say what might push us out. They are organised around the anatomy of a vol event: a spark (catalyst, policy, rate gap) becomes a vol event only if it hits fuel (positioning that gets hurt: IMM, carry stock, barriers, client flow) and an amplifier (dealer short gamma, structured exposure, thin liquidity); dampers (dealer long gamma, vol supply, level-based flows) absorb it; and premium supply and demand sets what the surface does afterwards. The useful constraint is that option P&L is realised relative to implied: a signal the surface already prices adds nothing unless it is mispriced, so leading features earn their place by forecasting realised-minus-implied or transitions the surface has not absorbed, and the proprietary ones — flow, dealer gamma, the barrier book — are where the edge is most likely to be.

Stored energy — a gap between a price or position and its anchor, held by something temporary with a known weakness (an expiry, a pain threshold, a policy limit) — and feedback (whether a shock spreads or dies out) are kept as hypotheses and as desk language. The first draft's implementation (a closure weight peaking when a gap's half-life matches the tenor; a Hawkes branching ratio as a fragility gauge) is parked: the weight was not derived from expected P&L, and Hawkes estimates are spuriously near-critical under time-varying baseline intensity, which is what regime change is. Known release dates survive as calendar-class covariates. Each leading feature is added one at a time, with a declared future path, and retained only if it improves out-of-sample transition likelihood and horizon-EV scoring beyond a baseline that already uses the continuous state.

12The horizon ladder built · validated on synthetic

The product. For each component, per pair and tenor, with today's named state as the conditioning: the cumulative P&L of past fresh entries at each horizon — mean, 90% interval, outcome quantiles, probability of profit, expected shortfall — with effective N after overlap and the count of independent episodes. Means are shrunk slightly toward the all-states mean when evidence is thin; tails are never shrunk. Intervals come from a circular block bootstrap with blocks about twice the horizon, which the synthetic validation shows is honest.

Regime dependence is the empirical split of each horizon's outcomes into entries whose state persisted and entries whose state broke, with the break frequency: (1 − q)·EV_stayed + q·EV_broke = EV exactly. It explains the headline rather than adjusting it, and it tells apart a component hurt by a break from one that is insurance against it, which the EV column cannot. It is never multiplied, never a ratio.

13The path model and repricer designed · not yet built

The ladder answers for a fresh unit in today's state. It cannot answer four things: the value of an existing position of arbitrary age and moneyness; the effect of today's leading signals where today's transition propensity differs from the state's average; horizons the data cannot reach; and designed stress scenarios. The path model answers those by generating market paths and repricing the actual position.

Crisis-state blocks come from a handful of shared episodes, so crisis paths are a declared blend of historical bootstrap and designed stress scenarios, labelled as such. The model needs two things from the backtester owners that do not exist yet — second-order Greek buckets and a surface-override capability — and one thing from itself: before any output is used, run from historical entry dates with the base matrix, it must reproduce the Phase 3 ladder within Monte Carlo error at every horizon.

14Validation and gates built · validated on synthetic

Every layer must beat the one below it out of sample, at each horizon, or the build stops at the highest layer that adds value. All selection — features, boundaries, smoothing, hysteresis, shrinkage, block length — happens inside training folds; the final holdout is looked at once.

LayerWhat it isWhat beating it shows
0Unconditional statistics at each horizonConditioning on anything helps
1A direct regularised model of h-day P&L on the small continuous state vectorDiscretising into states helps beyond the continuous state. If not, states become presentation language over a continuous model — an acceptable outcome
2The named-state ladder — the Phase 3 productThe go/no-go gate: 2 beats 0 and 1
2bThe ladder conditioned on discovered sub-states where they existA sub-state may enter the number only if 2b beats 2
3Path model with a constant matrix, for new tradesThe simulator adds value beyond measurement — expected mainly for existing positions and tails
4Time-varying transitions with leading features under a stated covariate policyLeading information has incremental value
GateCriterion (pre-registered, owner-only)Synthetic, true labelsSynthetic, estimated labels
1 · IntegrityAll integrity checks pass; hand-verified golden trades reproducepasspass
2 · SeparationAt h ≤ 10, entry states separate outcomes with stable sign in ≥ 75% of cellspasspass
3 · Go / no-goOut of sample at h ≤ 10, the ladder beats layers 0 and 1: positive MSE improvement, positive rank IC, calibration slope in [0.5, 1.5]fail (4 of 6 synthetic histories pass; misses are on the weakest component's slope)fail

Scoring is on rank correlation, calibration intercept and slope, a proper scoring loss, interval coverage, and sensitivity to removing each stress episode. Tail statistics are scored jointly (VaR and ES) with the low power stated plainly: two years of holdout hold about one observation in a 5% tail at one-month horizon. And the test that matters most is not statistical: in a shadow period, with the card visible to half the desk, do traders tilt composition differently?

15Open question: age dependence hypothesis

Preliminary inspection of real backtester output for the risk reversal shows mean daily P&L varying systematically with days since entry, with a shape that depends on tenor, and the pattern survives normalisation by current exposure. Under a stationary market with fixed exposure it would be flat. The leading explanation is that an aged position sits at a different point on the term structure of risk premia — a one-month risk reversal at day 18 is economically a three-day one, and short-dated VRP, skew dynamics and event weight all differ — with attribution artefacts at drifted strikes second. The diagnostic is a collapse test.

16What this is not

  1. Not a trade signal. A conditional description of what a component has earned, with its uncertainty and its evidence count. Composition is the trader's.
  2. Not a forecast of regime change. The regime-dependence split uses what happened; forward-looking tilts are Phase 5 and enter only through the transition matrix, only if they survive their test.
  3. Not a model of existing positions. The ladder is for a fresh unit; increments approximate aged ones; repricing an actual aged position is Phase 4.
  4. Not more states than the data can carry. Five named states, calibrated on ten years of surface; sub-states only where they are stable and only in the number if they beat their parent.
  5. Not production. About 1,900 lines of research code with 49 tests. If it earns its keep, it is rebuilt properly from the model guide.
